definitions: The quality of something is often directly related to its price; cheaper items may be of lower quality.
It is worth spending more money to get something of better quality.
examples: I bought a really cheap phone, but it broke in a month. I guess you get what you pay for.
Don't skimp on the car repairs; you get what you pay for.
Her new designer bag was expensive, but it's lasted for years. She always says you get what you pay for.
lemma: you get what you pay for
source: you get what you pay for
